description.narrative: Borno State is currently experiencing one of its largest cholera outbreaks in recent years, with over 14,700 suspected cases and 115 deaths reported as of June 2026. Transmission remains active, particularly in densely populated urban settlements, IDP camps, hostcommunities, and hard-to-reach areas such as Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC) and Konduga. These areas remain highly vulnerabledue to population movement, inadequate access to safe water, poor sanitation infrastructure, overcrowding, and weak hygiene practices. In response, Oxfam proposes an integrated cholera prevention and response intervention aimed at reducing transmission, strengthening community-level preparedness, and improving access to safe WASH services. The intervention will combine community engagement, rapid response mechanisms, and WASH improvements in both communities and health facilities, complementing the Government-led response.

participating-org.narrative:
Care Aid Support Initiative was founded in 2018 by a team of Humanterian and protection professionals in response to the humanitarian crisis in Northeast Nigeria. Principal stages: 2018-2019: Emergency phase - Mobile health clinics and WASH in 3 IDP camps in Maiduguri and Jere. 2020-2022: Expanded to GBV case management, SRHR, and psychosocial support. Integrated gender by recruiting 70%female frontline staff and establishing women-led community structures. 2023-2026: Transition to resilience and systems strengthening. Added climate-resilient WASH, civic engagement, and disability inclusion. Formalized partnerships with DPOs and LGA authorities. Major change: Shifted from pure humanitarian response to a rights-based, gender transformative approach that puts women, girls, youth and PWDs at the center of program design and governance.

ACHIEVEMENTS What have been the principal results in the past three years that contribute to significant, structural, sustained and positive improvement in the lives of men, women, girls and boys suffering from poverty, injustice, insecurity and exclusion? Some of the key achievement in the last three years include Key results contributing to structural improvement: Health <(>&<)> Protection: Reached 58,000 people with integrated health, GBV and SRHR services. 65% were women and girls. 1,240 GBV survivors received case management and referrals. WASH <(>&<)> Resilience: Rehabilitated 5climate-resilient boreholes and 12 gender-segregated latrines in flood-prone wards.Contributed to 25% reduction in cholera cases in2024 outbreak per SMoH data. Civic Engagement: Established 6 women’s groups and 4 youth networks that now co-lead community scorecards in 2 LGAs, resulting in 3 health facilities extending opening hours for women. Inclusion: Trained 120 community advocates including 35 persons with disabilities. PWD representation in LGA planning forums increased from 0% to 18%. 3. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE Mission: What is the current purpose of the organisation? We envision a society where the poor and vulnerable have access to social justice and sustainable livelihood. ORGANIZATIONAL MISSION To help people, families, and communities most affected by crises, violence, abuse, and natural disasters. Based in Nigeria,their work focuses on empowering vulnerable populations, promoting well-being, and providing basic needs such as secure shelter. Institutional objectives: What are the principal changes the organisation seeks to achieve over the long term?  Increase equitable access to quality health, GBV, and SRHR services for marginalized groups.  Strengthen community-led accountability and participation in local governance.  Build climate and shock resilience of vulnerable households in Northeast Nigeria.
Field(s) of activity: What are the principal thematic and geographic areas in which the organisation works? Who are the social actors that benefit from the work? Thematic areas: Health, GBV, SRHR, WASH, Climate Resilience, Civic Space, Disability Inclusion Geographic areas: Borno State - Maiduguri, Jere, and Dikwa LGAs Beneficiaries: IDPs, host communities, women, adolescent girls, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. . 4. STRATEGIC POSITIONING Analyse the environment in which the organisation works? Who are the other relevant social actors, including government and business, and what roles do they play? ' In this context, what is unique about the position of the organisation? Care Aid operates in a protracted humanitarian and shrinking civic space in Borno.
 Government: Borno SPHCDA, LGA Health Departments, Ministry of Women Affairs - duty bearers and service co-implementers.
 UN/INGOs: UNFPA, UNICEF, WHO, IRC - coordination through Health, WASH, GBV and Protection clusters.
 Community actors: Traditional and religious leaders, women-led CSOs, DPOs, youth groups - critical for access, legitimacy and norm change. Private sector: Limited engagement, potential for CSR in WASH.
What is unique: Care Aid is oneof few local NGOs with female leadership that combines direct service delivery with community accountability mechanisms. Our grassroots women’s groups provide direct feedback to LGA authorities, ensuring marginalized voices influence decisions.
